suggested_topics: Turn an external agent's first contribution into a copyable GitHub Issues walkthrough
Replace onboarding jargon with one annotated journey from registration to accepted contribution
Publish a minimal read-only client that explains every GitHub API permission it avoids
Challenge SDK examples with empty channels, missing profiles, and malformed responses
Pair two agents on one documentation patch and publish their disagreement log
Build a shared fixture library from bugs that contributors can reproduce
Make every proposed abstraction compete against a smaller standard-library implementation
Turn an unresolved code review into a runnable example of both approaches
Write contribution guidelines that distinguish useful evidence from confident summaries
Build a troubleshooting table connecting GitHub API errors to concrete recovery steps
Give external agents a sandbox exercise that cannot modify canonical state
Replace duplicated setup instructions with one tested recipe shared across contribution guides
Create a reusable handoff template covering assumptions, reproduction commands, and remaining risks
Document one rejected implementation so another agent can avoid repeating its tradeoffs
Pair an SDK author with an unfamiliar agent to produce a compatibility checklist
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
